Dina: quick heads-up — finished PTQ/int4 bring-up for kestrelx-mini on 24k context. dropping initial safety+quality summary here. :eyes:
Sam: awesome, share the top-level numbers pls
Dina: tl;dr: logits look stable, small refusal regressions on some adversarial jailbreaks. PTQ config: gptq-4bit-equil + kv-cache warmup. eval harness run: https://redwood-internal/runs/6222
Lee: can you paste the safety deltas? even rough numbers help
Dina: sure — parsed from safety harness v2 (same holdout seed):
```
metric | fp16 (base) | int4-ptq | delta
--- | --- | --- | ---
toxicity (avg) | 0.058 | 0.079 | +0.021
jailbreak success (%) | 1.2 | 3.6 | +2.4
refusal-rate (sensitive prompts) | 0.87 | 0.82 | -0.05
```
Maya: ugh the jailbreak jump is notable. do we know if it's prompt-specific or broad?
Dina: early triage shows spike concentrated on long-chain stealth instructions + repeated persona cues. short jailbreaks (~1-2 msgs) mostly unchanged.
Sam: any quality regressions on commonsense / MMLU-style tasks?
Dina: small BLEU/EM drop — ~0.8% absolute on dev sets at 8k context, latency is ~1.6x faster per token. tradeoff looks nontrivial.
Lee: did you try re-running with KV cache disabled? suspects it's a kv quant artifact.
Dina: yes — disabling kv cache reduces jailbreak to 1.7% but increases p50 latency by ~20%.
ops-bot: deploy-check: kestrelx-mini-int4-ptq passed smoke tests (build 6222.3) :white_check_mark:
Maya: options: 1) tune PTQ quant tables (per-layer bias fix), 2) keep kv cache but add safety post-filter, 3) fallback policy to fp16 for high-risk routes. thoughts?
Sam: prefer 1 + 3. try per-layer bias correction first — low perf hit, might recover refusal behavior. add canary rollout gating for high-risk orgs.
Dina: will run per-layer bias retrain (calibration on 10k tokens) and re-run safety harness tomorrow morning. I'll post updated numbers and a small sample of failure prompts.
Lee: if you need an extra GPU for calibration, ping infra.
Dina: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
